title: feat(objectql,service-storage): a refused sys_file reader sees a field-owned file's metadata by the download door's verdict (#22637)
body:
Fixes #22637
Clause-②: yes

## What changes

A reader who may read a record but not `sys_file` (the default: `member_default` grants no `sys_file` read) used to get every file field back as `{ id, metadataRefused: true }` (PR #22620). The download door judges the same file by the record that owns it (ADR-0104 D3) and served that reader the bytes. So the reader could download the file but could not see its name.

This executes the maintainer's ruling B on #22624, verbatim as the card records it:

> A file field's metadata follows the parent-derived verdict the download door already applies (ADR-0104 D3, `buildFileReadAuthorizer`): when the caller's `sys_file` read is refused, `resolveFileReferences` still hydrates a file whose `ref_object` / `ref_id` name the record being read (the delegate consulted where the owner object declares a `fileAccessDelegate`); a referenced id that does not point at that record keeps PR #22620's refused marker; direct `sys_file` queries and `public_read` are unchanged.

- **From.** A reader with read on `contract` and no `sys_file` read gets `{ "signed_pdf": { "id": "f_7cQx2Lm90a", "metadataRefused": true } }`.
- **To.** For a file whose `ref_object` / `ref_id` name the record being read, that reader gets `{ id, name, size, mimeType, url }`, exactly what a `sys_file` reader gets, when the door's field-owned verdict allows. A delegate-governed object gets the delegate's answer.
- **Unchanged.**
  - Every other id keeps the marker: an id copied in from another record, an attachment-only or unclaimed file, a `public_read` file the record does not own, and an owned file the verdict refuses.
  - `sys_file`'s own read rule: a direct `sys_file` query by the same reader is still `PERMISSION_DENIED` (403).
  - `public_read` handling.
  - A `sys_file` reader's hydration.
  - The download door's verdict for every request.
  - An engine with no verdict registered.

## One verdict, two callers

`ObjectQL` holds no service registry (no `getService` or kernel reference in `engine.ts`), so the engine cannot reach a declared `fileAccessDelegate` itself. Copying "delegate declared, so ask it and fail closed; otherwise read the record" into the engine would be the second predicate the ruling forbids. The verdict stays where it is and is handed over, the same way `registerHeldFileResolver` already hands over the tombstone holder question:

- **`service-storage`** (`storage-service-plugin.ts`)
  - The field-owned arm of `buildFileReadAuthorizer` (the `:1237`-`:1265` range the ruling cites) moves, unchanged, into one module-private batched function, `readableFieldOwners(registry, engine, ownerObject, ownerIds, authz)`. It is not exported from the package.
  - The door calls it with its one owner id. The query is byte-identical (`where: { id }`, `fields: ['id']`, `limit: 1`, any row allows), and so is the fail-closed handling of the delegate.
  - `start()` registers the same function on the engine, beside `registerHeldFileResolver`, through the new duck-typed seam `registerFieldOwnedFileReadAuthorizer`.
- **`objectql`** (`engine.ts`)
  - The new seam is `registerFieldOwnedFileReadAuthorizer` (type `FieldOwnedFileReadAuthorizer`, exported).
  - On the refused arm of `resolveFileReferences`, `readParentDerivedFiles` makes two reads.
    1. One `sys_file` read in a `sudo()`-shaped context (`{ ...caller, isSystem: true }`, so the tenant wall and the transaction ride along). Its `where` asks for the ownership pair itself (`id $in`, `ref_object` this object, `ref_id $in` this result's record ids) and projects only seven columns.
    2. One call to the registered verdict with every owner id, under the caller's envelope minus its operation-private `__` keys (`withoutOperationPrivateKeys`).
  - Allowed rows go through the same servability rule as the normal path (`servableFileRows`, extracted, shared) and render through one `toFileValue`.
  - Judged per element and per record: an id hydrates only on the record whose field owns it.
  - Unwired, a projection without `id`, or any failure: every id keeps the marker. A failure logs one `warn`.

**Is the ownership match a second predicate?** No, by the ruling's own words. "Whose `ref_object` / `ref_id` name the record being read" is the ruling's scope condition, not an access verdict. The verdict is reached without a copy: the door's own function decides allow or deny, including the delegate. The system read is the posture the door already reads a file in (by id, system context, never the caller's `sys_file` grant). It serves only ids a record the caller just read holds.

The read is deliberately narrower than the door, by the ruling. The door also serves a file's uploader and any file reachable through a `sys_attachment` parent. Hydration serves only a file owned by the record being read.

## Measured on `main` first

The test was a scratch file in `plugin-security`, never committed and deleted after the run. It used real `ObjectQL` (source), the real `SecurityPlugin`, the real `StorageServicePlugin` and `SqlDriver`. The reader had read on the record's object and no `sys_file` read. Two committed files were seeded: one field-owned by record `d1`, and one owned by `d9` and copied into `d2`.

- With `engine.ts` and `storage-service-plugin.ts` at `243dd3c625` (blobs `3177422431` and `0246a5bfe4`): `d1` read `{ id, metadataRefused: true }`, `d2` read `{ id, metadataRefused: true }`, and a direct `sys_file` query got `PERMISSION_DENIED` / 403. The premise holds on `main`.
- At this branch: `d1` read `{ id, name: 'contract.pdf', size: 1024, mimeType: 'application/pdf', url }`, `d2` still read `{ id, metadataRefused: true }`, and the direct query still got `PERMISSION_DENIED` / 403.
- The two files were restored from `HEAD`: blob equals `HEAD`, `git diff HEAD` is empty, and the porcelain status is clean.

## Pins

- `packages/services/service-storage/src/field-owned-file-hydration-door-agreement.test.ts` (new). Both surfaces are asked about one fixture: the door is `GET /files/:fileId/url` as the reader, and the record read runs as the same reader. The fixture is one real `ObjectQL` + `SqlDriver`, with `StorageServicePlugin` booted and wired as it ships.
  - A field-owned file on the record read: the door returns 200 and the read hydrates in full.
  - A `fileAccessDelegate` that refuses: the door returns 403 `FILE_DOWNLOAD_DENIED` and the read keeps the marker. A delegate that allows: the door returns 200 and the read hydrates, and the delegate was asked by the reader for the owning record. Both decisions are readable by a raw record read, so the delegate is what decides.
  - An id copied out of a record the reader cannot read: refused on both surfaces.
  - The ruling's boundary: an id copied from a record the reader can read hydrates on its owner and keeps the marker where it was copied. An attachment-only file keeps the marker.
  - `public_read` is unchanged: anonymous door 200, and the refused reader's read keeps the marker.
  - A direct `sys_file` query is still refused. A multi-value field is judged per element.
  - Stand-ins: the `sys_file` refusal (middleware throwing `PERMISSION_DENIED`, the shape `plugin-security`'s `file-field-hydration-refused.test.ts` measures on the real layer), the permission store (unregistered objects read empty), and authentication by header.
- `packages/objectql/src/engine-file-hydrate-parent-derived.test.ts` (new) covers the engine's half with a recorded stand-in verdict:
  - per-record pairing, mixed arrays, another object's same id, and a refusing verdict;
  - the verdict is asked once, with owner ids only and no `__` keys, and exactly one system `sys_file` read is made, with the ownership pair in its `where`;
  - an owned tombstone (held) and a pending upload, each read as a `sys_file` reader reads it, and a projection without `id`;
  - unwired, a failing system read and a throwing verdict (marker plus one `warn`);
  - controls: a `sys_file` reader, a direct `sys_file` query, an empty field.
- Unedited and green: the door's existing tests (`mount-storage-routes`, `storage-routes`, `file-read-tenancy-posture-admission`, `storage-routes.authz-outage-relay` and the rest of `service-storage`), plus #22620's `engine-file-hydrate-refused.test.ts` and `plugin-security/src/file-field-hydration-refused.test.ts`.

## Ablation

`node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` (WRAP mode) replaced the anchor `const owned = await this.readParentDerivedFiles(objectName, records, uniqueIds, execCtx);` with the same call over `records.slice(0, 0)` plus a `debug` marker line. That removes the parent-derived arm. The anchor hit once (1 to 0), and the blob changed from `6a9455a5d3` to `bb576869bc`.

- **objectql** (the test imports `./engine`, so it reads source): 10 failed and 6 passed. The first pin received `{ id: 'f_owned_1aa', metadataRefused: true }`. The failing-read and throwing-verdict cases went red too: with the arm gone, nothing is read, so their `warn` never comes.
- **service-storage** (`@objectstack/objectql` resolves to `dist/`, a `KNOWN_UNALIASED_TEST_IMPORTS` pair): `objectql` was rebuilt with the mutation, and `ablation-dist-preflight` found the marker in 4 built files. Result: 4 failed and 5 passed. The field-owned pin received `{ id, metadataRefused: true }`, and the delegate-allow, owner-side-of-a-copy and multi-value pins failed too. The refusal-side pins stayed green, as they should.
- **Restore.** The blob equals `HEAD` (`6a9455a5d3`), `git diff HEAD` is empty, and the porcelain status is clean. After a rebuild, `ablation-dist-preflight --absent` passed (marker absent from all 14 built files, tree clean), and both files went green again: 16 of 16 and 9 of 9.

The ablation ran at `e6e7fbec66`. The merge of `origin/main` that followed did not change `engine.ts`, the `service-storage` package or either new test (the `git diff --stat` is empty).

## Verification at `9931bb55d3` (head, `origin/main` merged)

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/objectql exec vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2`: 394 files, 7753 tests passed. `--project repo`: 1 file, 5 tests passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/service-storage exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2`: 51 files, 846 tests passed.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/plugin-security exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 src/file-field-hydration-refused.test.ts`: 4 passed.
- `typecheck`: `@objectstack/objectql` passed (exit 0; test layer 40 files / 234 errors / 65 pinned signatures, unchanged), and `@objectstack/service-storage` passed (exit 0; test layer clean).
- Gates: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands` (no paths) derives 102 commands. All 102 ran after a full `turbo run build`, each with its exit code captured before any pipe, and all exited 0. `--ran` reconciles them as 102 derived, 102 run, 0 NOT MEASURED. Two red results on the first pass were real and are fixed: `check:query-options-erasure` (my tests erased query options, 236 to 240, now 236) and `check:slot-lookup` (a `getService` typed `any` in my test).
- Lint, a narrowed run: `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 5 changed `.ts` files reports 5 files, 0 errors and 0 warnings.
  - Population: `eslint.config.mjs`, the config `pnpm lint` (`eslint .`) runs.
  - Invariance: the config enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project`), so this diff cannot move any untouched file's verdict.

## Cross-lane paths

Declared before any edit:

- **`domain:services`**, on #6021 (comment 6097907456):
  - `packages/services/service-storage/src/storage-service-plugin.ts`: the extraction and the engine registration;
  - `packages/services/service-storage/src/field-owned-file-hydration-door-agreement.test.ts`: new.
- **`domain:devx`**, on #6023 (comment 6098008938), prose only:
  - `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx`: the `file` read forms;
  - `content/docs/permissions/attachments-access.mdx`: the refused-reader clause.

No generated page and no `content/docs/releases/` path.

## Acceptance notes

- **`FileRefusedValueSchema`'s TSDoc** (`packages/spec`, "when the reader is refused the `sys_file` read that resolves it") is left as it is. It is now a slight overstatement: the marker means the read was refused and the parent-derived verdict did not allow it. Changing it would pull in `gen:schema` / `gen:docs`. The same holds for `fileAccessDelegate`'s TSDoc and `.describe()` ("authorizes downloads"). The delegate is now also consulted for a refused reader's metadata. Neither is false; both are incomplete.
- **Narrower than the door.** An uploader without `sys_file` read, reading a delegate-governed record whose delegate refuses them, sees the marker although the door serves them the bytes (the door's owner arm). The ruling cites the field-owned arm only.
- **A projection that leaves out `id`** cannot name its owner record, so every id keeps the marker. Not measured: whether any shipped caller projects file fields without `id`.
- **Cost.** A refused hydration with owned ids makes one more system `sys_file` read and one verdict call: one batched owner read, or one delegate call per owner. The non-delegate arm re-reads records the caller has just read. That is redundant by construction (the ruling's own reduction), and it is the price of one predicate.
- **No committed pin drives the full composition** (real `SecurityPlugin` + `StorageServicePlugin` + REST). The scratch measurement above did, uncommitted. A dogfood pin would live in `packages/qa` (`domain:cli`) and is not in this PR. Carrier: none.
